free_tier.stated: Free accounts are capped at 10,000 stored contents — uploads past the cap fail with `error-limits`.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The API reference, FAQ and Premium page state no per-file size limit; the free-account limit stated is a count of 10,000 stored contents.

retention.stated: Content is kept for 10 days of inactivity, and stays longer as long as it keeps being downloaded.
retention.notes: Content past its storage period may be moved to cold storage instead of deleted; importing it back requires Premium.

egress.terms: Free traffic may be counted by IP address, so on a shared IP other people's downloads can count toward the usage shown. Bandwidth is not throttled; over the allowance some download functionality is restricted.

interface_detail: rest; rclone (the FAQ names an official rclone implementation)
tooling: REST API at api.gofile.io (documented, CORS, per-endpoint rate limits); rclone backend 'gofile' (Tier 1) but its docs warn 'if you wish to connect rclone to Gofile you will need a premium account'; guest account creation is a single unauthenticated POST
chaining: An upload without a token creates a guest account and returns a guestToken to reuse; the API reference says to create one account and reuse its token, not one per upload. Each free account is capped at 10,000 stored contents. A separate traffic allowance per guest account is not stated.

limits.value: Content is kept for 10 days of inactivity, and stays longer as long as it keeps being downloaded.

limits_note: content is deleted after 10 days of inactivity unless it keeps being downloaded; past the storage period content may be moved to cold storage and importing it back requires Premium; most API endpoints (listing, direct links) return error-notPremium; 'Repeatedly exceeding rate limits may result in automatic IP bans'
reliability_note: 10-day inactivity expiry plus cold-storage migration makes it storage-with-a-TTL, not a drive; content-count cap (10k) bites hard on many-small-file datasets
confidence_note: the API page states the 10,000-content cap on a free account

extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-10
extras.quota_verbatim: no storage figure at all on the free tier — free accounts get temporary storage with a 10,000-content cap per account ('Free accounts are capped at 10,000 stored contents'); free traffic allowance is '100 GB traffic / 30 days'
extras.limits_verbatim: content is deleted after 10 days of inactivity unless it keeps being downloaded; past the storage period content may be moved to cold storage and importing it back requires Premium; most API endpoints (listing, direct links) return error-notPremium; 'Repeatedly exceeding rate limits may result in automatic IP bans'
extras.egress_verbatim: free plan: '100 GB traffic / 30 days'; 'We never throttle bandwidth' but traffic over the allowance restricts download functionality. Premium removes caps entirely
extras.chaining_verbatim: unlimited guest accounts created by API call (no email, no human-verification step) x 10,000 files each — probe-verified; each guest account also brings its own 100 GB/30-day traffic bucket, so fetch load can be sharded by account
extras.tooling_verbatim: REST API at api.gofile.io (documented, CORS, per-endpoint rate limits); rclone backend 'gofile' (Tier 1) but its docs warn 'if you wish to connect rclone to Gofile you will need a premium account'; guest account creation is a single unauthenticated POST
extras.agent_focus: niche/regional/small consumer drives with >=500GB free, plus 'unlimited' lifetime-deal cloud and free Nextcloud hosts

binding_note: a clock, not a quota: bytes leave whether or not transfer is completed
